meta.title: Rollout – Zwift & MyWhoosh on Steam Deck and Bazzite
meta.description: Play Zwift and MyWhoosh on Steam Deck, SteamOS and Bazzite. Rollout installs, updates and starts them with a controller. Download, double-click, ride.

apps.title: Pick your ride.
apps.sub: Each app gets the setup that works best on Linux. Rollout picks it for you.
apps.mw.1: Trainer and heart-rate strap over Bluetooth, paired in the game like on Windows
apps.mw.2: Runs with GE-Proton, downloaded and verified for you
apps.zw.1: Runs in a container from netbrain/zwift, kept apart from your system
apps.zw.2: Sensors connect through Zwift Companion on your phone or Direct Connect, not directly over Bluetooth
apps.zw.3: Your controller steers the game in Gaming Mode
feat.title: Built for the couch and the saddle.
f0.d: Every screen works with gamepad, touch and keyboard. Menus and lists are Rollout's own, so they work in Gaming Mode where native popups don't.
f1.d: No mandatory questions, no terminal, no sudo. Rollout shows size and time up front, then clear phases with progress.
f2.d: Rollout can update itself in the background. Every launcher update is signed and test-started; if it fails, Rollout goes back to the last good version on its own.
f3.d: One switch adds Rollout and your apps to Steam, with artwork. Start rides straight from Gaming Mode; play time survives updates.
f4.d: For MyWhoosh, the Bluetooth check shows which trainers and heart-rate straps are sending before you clip in, and can restart a stuck adapter.
f5.d: When something goes wrong, Rollout says what to do next in plain words, with one button to try again. Details only if you want them.
f6.d: Behind “Advanced”: Proton version, graphics output, Bluetooth adapter, update channel, logs and diagnostics. Every option shows the recommended value.
ex1.d: Follows your system, switch any time.
ex3.d: Light and dark, interface size up to 200 %. Readable from the saddle.
ex4.d: No root, no system packages. Your OS stays as it is.
dl.title: Double-click. Ride.
dl.sub: Pick your system, download Rollout and open it in Desktop Mode. No terminal needed.
dl.beta: Beta: tested on ROG Ally with Bazzite. Steam Deck not yet verified.
dl.bazzite.dev: ROG Ally, other handhelds, desktop PCs
dl.file: Starter file, installs Rollout into your home folder
dl.s1: Steam button → Power → Switch to Desktop
dl.s3: Confirm the prompt once. Rollout appears in your app menu.
dl.b1: On a handheld, switch to Desktop Mode. On a PC you are already there.
dl.steamos.note: Zwift also needs Podman or Docker, which SteamOS usually does not include. MyWhoosh needs neither.
dl.bazzite.note: Podman is included, which Zwift needs. Bazzite with GNOME: downloaded .desktop files do not start by double-click there, so this install does not work on that edition yet. Use the KDE edition.
dl.other: Other Linux distributions: not supported, at your own risk. See GitHub.
how.title: Thin launcher. Proven engines.
how.sub: Rollout does not patch games. It drives open projects that already do the hard work.
how.1d: Upstream scripts are pinned to an exact commit and checked with SHA-256. Launcher updates are signed with Ed25519.
how.2d: Rollout lives in ~/.local/share/rollout. Installing needs no root and changes no system packages on SteamOS or Bazzite.
how.3d: Zwift has no direct Bluetooth in its container, and neither game is officially supported on Linux. Rollout says so instead of hiding it.
faq.title: Questions riders ask.
faq.1.q: Does Zwift run on Steam Deck and Bazzite?
faq.1.a: On Bazzite it does: Zwift runs in a container based on netbrain/zwift, which Rollout installs and starts. Rollout is tested on a ROG Ally with Bazzite; the Steam Deck is not yet verified. SteamOS usually needs Podman or Docker first. Sensors connect through Zwift Companion on your phone or Direct Connect, not directly over Bluetooth.
faq.2.q: Does MyWhoosh run on SteamOS and Linux with Bluetooth?
faq.2.a: Yes. MyWhoosh runs with GE-Proton and talks to your trainer and heart-rate strap over Bluetooth directly. You pair them in the game, like on Windows.
faq.3.q: Does Zwift work on the ROG Ally?
faq.3.a: Yes, on Bazzite. Install Rollout in Desktop Mode, then start Zwift from Rollout or from Steam in Gaming Mode. Your controller steers the game.
faq.4.a: No. Download Rollout.desktop, double-click it in Desktop Mode and confirm once. Rollout then appears in your app menu.
faq.5.a: Yes. Rollout works with gamepad, touch and keyboard. In Gaming Mode your controller also steers Zwift.
faq.6.a: Rollout checks for new versions in the background and installs them automatically if you want. Launcher updates are signed, and a broken update rolls back on its own.
faq.7.q: Is Rollout official? Can my account get banned?
faq.7.a: No. Rollout is an independent project, not affiliated with Zwift, Inc., MyWhoosh or Valve. Their terms restrict unapproved third-party tools, and they can suspend accounts at their discretion. Read the terms and decide for yourself.
faq.8.q: Which devices and systems are supported?
faq.8.a: Rollout is in beta. It is tested on a ROG Ally with Bazzite. SteamOS on the Steam Deck is the second target but not yet verified. Other Linux distributions are at your own risk.
